title: Heartbeat-driven idle connection reclamation and partial-output reconciliation
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Long-lived client connections can become idle or abruptly disconnect during multi-token streaming generations. Without a robust reclamation and reconciliation mechanism we observe: leaked in-flight allocations, orphaned KV prefixes retained in cache, skewed telemetry (inflated open sessions), and customer-visible partial outputs with no clear reconciliation path. This ticket designs and implements a heartbeat-driven reclamation circuit plus a deterministic partial-output reconciliation flow that works across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments and preserves existing API compatibility.
motivation_and_goals: 1) Reclaim resources quickly for stalled/abandoned streaming generations while avoiding false-positive tear-downs for legitimately slow clients. 2) Provide a clear API-level reconciliation for partially emitted outputs so clients and downstream tool-calling handlers can decide to resume, restart, or mark as final. 3) Emit telemetry and traces that make post-mortem and SLO attribution straightforward.
proposal_summary: Introduce a lightweight client heartbeat (over existing streaming channel) with optional server-side watchdog. On missed heartbeats beyond adaptive thresholds the server moves the generation into a "+\"quiescent\"+" state where KV prefixes and ephemeral buffers are checkpointed and short-term retained (configurable TTL). A reconciliation endpoint /resume-generation (internal-first) will accept a resume token allowing clients to reattach and pick up from the latest checkpoint. For public API compatibility we add: 1) an opt-in header X-RW-Stream-Heartbeat-Interval for client SDKs; 2) a server-side autoset default based on route SLOs; 3) a generation-state lifecycle that surfaces 'in_progress', 'quiesced', 'finalized', 'abandoned' to the Console and telemetry. Garbage collection for quiesced generations runs via TTL and a circuit-breaker that prevents mass eviction during high churn.
design_decisions: Use heartbeats piggybacked on existing streaming frames to avoid a separate control channel
Adaptive threshold: combine client-configured heartbeat interval and recent token emission rate to compute timeout
Quiesced state preserves KV cache prefixes and last emitted token index; state must be compact and encrypted at rest in Private deployments
Expose resume token as base64 opaque string; do not expand schema for public consumption to avoid coupling
Introduce server-side circuit-breaker: if GC reclaim rate exceeds 5% of active generations per minute, throttle reclamation and escalate to ops
Do not change current non-streaming completion semantics; this is additive for streaming only to maintain compatibility
api_changes_and_compatibility:
- New optional header: X-RW-Stream-Heartbeat-Interval (ms) accepted by hosted SDKs. If absent, server uses route defaults.
- New internal endpoint POST /internal/v1/resume-generation accepting resume token and client auth, returning current generation state and optionally a delta of lost tokens. This will be gated behind a feature flag for 2 months.
- Streaming frames augmented with a Heartbeat frame type (heartbeat frames carry minimal idx + timestamp). All existing frame types remain unchanged. SDKs will treat heartbeat frames as transparent if not understood.
storage_and_gc: Quiesced generation metadata stored in ephemeral store (Redis) with small on-disk tombstone in main store for cross-process discovery. Default quiesce TTL = 5 minutes; configurable per-route up to 24 hours for dedicated/private. GC runs in two phases: soft prune (delete ephemeral buffers, keep checkpoints) and hard prune (remove checkpoints). Soft prune runs after TTL; hard prune requires PCI and compliance approvals for >24h retention in Private installs.
observability_and_slos: Add metrics: rw.stream.heartbeats.missed, rw.stream.quiesced.count, rw.stream.resume.success, rw.stream.gc.soft_prune_count, rw.stream.gc.hard_prune_count. Trace spans mark generation lifecycle transitions. Create Grafana dashboards and an alert if missed-heartbeats for a route exceed 1% of active streams for 5m. Update token-level cost attribution to exclude quiesced retention windows beyond 2 minutes unless retention is extended by customer.
security_and_privacy: Resume tokens are single-use, encrypted, and short-lived. For Private deployments they are stored with KMS-wrapped keys. No resume token or quiesced checkpoint is ever emitted to customer logs by default; only metadata IDs are logged. Security review not required for initial rollout but required if retention >24h is enabled.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (canary): Implement heartbeat frames + server watchdog behind feature flag; roll to 5% of hosted traffic and Dedicated test pools. Duration: 2 weeks.
Phase 2 (SDK integration): Ship SDK changes to emit heartbeats (JS/Go/Python). Gate with feature flag allowing clients to opt-in. Duration: 3 weeks.
Phase 3 (resume endpoint): Enable internal resume endpoint for support-assisted recoveries; surface to customers as beta after 4 weeks.
Phase 4 (full): Expose header and enable default rollout. Monitor metrics and safety thresholds before enabling in Private installs with >24h retention.
Rollback: disable feature flag and run hard GC on any lingering quiesced states originating from canary within 48h.
acceptance_criteria: Heartbeat frames accepted by server and do not break legacy clients (verified via canary)
Missed-heartbeat detection reclaims >75% of orphaned in-flight allocations within 10s of threshold without false-positive >1% on healthy clients
Resume flow successfully reattaches client to quiesced generation in 90% of test cases with <=2 token re-emission
Telemetry surfaces quiesced->finalized transitions and dashboards show clear attribution for costs
No regression in p95 token latency across routes during canary
testing_plan: Unit tests for heartbeat parsing and timeout logic. Integration tests: simulate slow high-latency clients, abrupt TCP closes, and long-tail slow token consumption. Chaos test: mass client disconnects to validate GC circuit-breaker. E2E: SDK-run resume scenario replicating in-house QA harness. Load test to ensure additional heartbeat traffic does not meaningfully increase CPU on serving mesh.
implementation_tasks: Core runtime: accept heartbeat frame, update last-seen index (ENG runtime team)
Runtime: implement quiesce state and checkpoint export to ephemeral store
API: implement feature-flagged internal resume endpoint and resume-token generator
Console: show quiesced generations in debug view (ops only)
SDKs: opt-in heartbeat emission and transparent handling for older runtime versions
Observability: add metrics/traces and Grafana dashboard panels
Docs: update streaming API docs and migration notes

notes: This ticket focuses on streaming-only flows and explicitly does not change non-streaming completion semantics. We should coordinate with SDK owners early to minimize client churn. Consider providing a compatibility shim for older SDKs that will not send heartbeat frames by treating silence as normal but subject to longer timeouts.
